notes.claim: Where two lines cross, the coordinates of the crossing point are the solutions of the pair of equations; parallel lines never cross, so give no solution.
Equations with more than one unknown can have an infinite number of solutions, so another equation is needed alongside.
When the two equations are really the same line, there are infinitely many solutions.
A solution of a system is an ordered pair that makes both equations true.

sources.title: 4.1 Solve Systems of Linear Equations with Two Variables - Intermediate Algebra 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: To solve a system of two linear equations, we want to find the values of the variables that are solutions to both equations. In other words, we are looking for the ordered pairs that make both equations true.

sources.title: Solving simultaneous equations graphically - KS3 Maths - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: If the two lines cross, then the coordinates of this intersection are the solutions to the simultaneous equations. If the lines are parallel (and therefore do not intersect), there is no solution.

sources.title: Solving simultaneous equations - GCSE Maths Revision
sources.quote: Equations that have more than one unknown can have an infinite number of solutions.

sources.title: 4.1 Solve Systems of Linear Equations with Two Variables - Intermediate Algebra 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: When the two equations were really the same line, there were infinitely many solutions.
